headline: Netflix Releases VOID, a Model That Erases Objects and Their Consequences from Video
lede: Netflix has published its first open-weight AI model, **VOID** (*Video Object and Interaction Deletion*), on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 licence. Unlike conventional video-editing tools that can remove a foreground object while leaving its shadow or reflection intact, VOID also eliminates the physical knock-on effects — a falling item, a displaced prop — that the removed object would have caused. The release marks a rare step toward public disclosure from a studio that has historically treated its production technology as a competitive secret.
body:
The model's central insight is a distinction the field has largely elided: there are two kinds of secondary effects that appear when an object is present in a scene. *Secondary optical effects* — shadows, reflections, highlights — have been addressed by existing inpainting tools with varying success. But *physical interaction effects* — a box that falls because a person was leaning against it, or debris scattered by a deleted prop — are causally downstream of the removed object and require the model to reason about what *would have happened* had the object never been there. VOID is designed to handle both classes.

To do this, Netflix fine-tuned **CogVideoX-Fun-V1.5-5b-InP**, a 5-billion-parameter 3D Transformer video model developed by Zhipu AI, on what they call *interaction-aware quadmask conditioning*. Rather than a simple binary mask (remove / keep), the quadmask encodes four distinct regions: the primary object to delete, areas where it overlaps with other scene elements, regions physically *affected* by its presence (falling objects, displaced items), and background to preserve unchanged. Giving the model this richer annotation lets it learn to hallucinate plausible scene completion rather than simply filling a hole.

The model ships as two checkpoints. The first, `void_pass1.safetensors`, is the core inpainting model and sufficient for most clips. The second, `void_pass2.safetensors`, adds optical-flow-warped latent initialisation to improve *temporal consistency* — the tendency of diffusion-based video models to flicker or drift across frames — on longer sequences. Both run at 384×672 pixels and support up to 197 frames. The hardware bar is steep: the authors specify a GPU with at least 40 GB of VRAM, such as an NVIDIA A100, which limits near-term use to researchers and well-resourced studios rather than individual creators.

The accompanying paper (arXiv 2604.02296) and a public demo flesh out the technical claims, but the practical implications have drawn more immediate attention. High-quality object removal with coherent physical consequences would reduce a labour-intensive step in post-production — currently handled frame-by-frame by visual effects artists — and could eventually make practical-effects clean-up accessible at smaller budgets. One Hacker News commenter noted that the technology 'could totally change practical effects,' though the VRAM requirement means democratisation remains conditional on hardware costs falling further.

concepts.definition: The task of removing a region from a video and filling it with plausible content consistent with the surrounding scene across all frames. It is harder than image inpainting because the filled region must also be temporally consistent — not flickering or drifting — as the camera and scene move.

A four-value segmentation mask used as an additional input to VOID. Each pixel is assigned to one of four categories: the primary object to remove, its overlap with other objects, regions physically affected by the object's presence, or background to keep. This richer signal allows the model to handle both optical and physical secondary effects.

A quality property of video generation or editing models: generated pixels should not flicker, change colour arbitrarily, or drift between adjacent frames. Diffusion models applied frame-by-frame often lack this property; VOID's optional second pass uses optical flow to warp latent representations across time as a corrective.

An open-source video generation model from Zhipu AI built on a 3D Transformer architecture. Netflix used a 5-billion-parameter variant as the base model for VOID, fine-tuning it on video inpainting with the quadmask conditioning scheme.

repos.summary: The official repository for VOID, Netflix's video object and interaction deletion model. It includes a Jupyter notebook for end-to-end inference, CLI instructions, and links to the model checkpoints on Hugging Face. The repo requires a 40 GB+ VRAM GPU and provides a sample video for testing the removal pipeline.
